analyst_view.overall: Mallorca have not played in the league since beating Cádiz on 2 November because their game at Andorra was postponed, so Luis García's side arrive rested, sixth and with a game in hand. Córdoba beat Ceuta 3-0 last time out, with Diego Percan (six league goals) scoring twice. I found little fresh team news for this match this week, so the view rests mainly on form and LaLiga's season figures; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I have moved from higher to same: Mallorca's league games average under two goals (15 scored, 7 conceded in 12), while Córdoba's average more than three (22-22 in 13). Adrián Fuentes (seven goals) against a leaky Córdoba defence pulls one way, Mallorca's tight defence the other.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I keep a slight lean higher: Córdoba build a lot through crosses and have taken 154 shots in 13 games by LaLiga's count, the kind of attacking that wins corners even away, and Mallorca will have plenty of the ball at Son Moix.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. I lean a touch higher: LaLiga has Córdoba on 43 yellows, two reds and 208 fouls committed in 13 games, and they finished at Celta Fortuna with nine men two games ago. With no referee named yet, I would not go far above six.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots, with 15.0 for Mallorca. I have moved from same to lower: LaLiga counts Mallorca at only 109 shots in 12 games, among the fewest in the division, so their share looks high even at home. Córdoba should get their usual volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, which fits two sides with reliable finishers in Fuentes and Percan. Mallorca's low shot volume and Córdoba's open games roughly cancel out, so I lean neither way.
